global_rules: First viewport must feel tool-first, not marketing-first.
Avoid duplicated trust/privacy cues; one clear local-only cue is enough.
Hero layout must use a coherent grid and avoid large empty columns.
H1 and subtitle should belong to one visual text group.
Section labels should feel like integrated UI tokens/cards, not generic uppercase badges.
UI tokens such as section pills and privacy pills should be compact and must not compete with the primary tool.
H1 should be strong but not oversized compared with the actual tool.
Section pills, hero chips, and privacy pills should be compact UI tokens.
Section labels should support hierarchy without competing with tool controls.
Decorative illustration should not overpower the main tool.
Utility buttons should be smaller than primary action buttons and result values.
Manual visual edits must not automatically trigger QA unless the user explicitly asks.
calculator_family_rules: Calculator pages need a strong primary result area.
Inputs and outputs should be visually connected.
Supporting sections should share one consistent section label system.
Reset and helper controls should be visually smaller than primary results and form headings.
Helper content should not push the real calculator too far down.
Reset and helper controls should stay smaller than primary results.
sample_specific_rules: Use "401(k) Calculator" as the main H1.
Keep one local-only cue: "Runs locally in your browser. No sign-up. No personal data stored."
Remove duplicate "Local-only retirement estimate" hero badge.
Use a lightweight right-side support card when left-aligning the hero text would otherwise leave empty space.
Use numbered pill/card section labels: 01 Your assumptions, 02 Projection table, 03 Plain-English method, 04 Quick guide, 05 Questions.
confirmed_sizing_rules: Keep financial output numbers prominent; shrink headings, pills, and utility controls before shrinking primary result values.
